cases.statement: Two carriers, a brother and sister in one Japanese family (family 1): Patient 1 (proband, III-2, male, 35 y) and Patient 2 (younger sister, III-3, female, 34 y), both with childhood-onset Behçet-like disease. Neither text nor table says 'heterozygous' in words; the pedigree labels alleles as M1 or WT.

people.label: Patient 1
people.zygosity_or_genotype: not stated in words; one variant allele (M1) implied by the pedigree labelling
people.key_phenotypes: onset at 6 y with fever and lymphadenopathy; recurrent oral and perianal ulcers (diagnosed Behçet's disease at 7 y); recurrent high fever with lymphadenopathy, pharyngalgia and nausea; genital ulcers (Table 1); no ocular or neurological symptoms

quotes.quote: In patient 1, we identified a novel nonsense variant, c.1434C>A:p.(Cys478*), in TNFAIP3 (NM_006290.3).
Patient 1 (III-2 in Fig. 1a) is a 35-year-old male who is the second child of non-consanguineous Japanese parents.
He presented with fever and lymphadenopathy at the age of 6.
He was diagnosed with BD at 7 years of age because of recurrent oral and perianal ulcers and was prescribed with oral prednisolone (PSL).
He had recurrent episodes of high-grade fever (up to 39 °C) associated with lymphadenopathy, pharyngalgia, and nausea.
The TNFAIP3 alleles identified in each individual are labeled as M1 and M2 for variants and WT for wild-type.

people.label: Patient 2
people.zygosity_or_genotype: not stated in words; Sanger-confirmed carrier of the same variant
people.key_phenotypes: oral ulcers at 12 y and genital ulcers at 15 y; recurrent fever and erythema nodosum; gastric and colonic ulcers; hepatosplenomegaly and generalized lymphadenopathy; Raynaud's phenomenon and pernio-like rash

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the same variant in the affected sister (patient 2) (Fig. 1a).
Patient 2 (III-3 in Fig. 1a) is the proband’s younger sister.
She had oral and genital ulcers at 12 and 15 years of age, respectively.
Gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed multiple ulcers in the stomach and colon, which were not typical of intestinal BD (Fig. 4d, e).
Torso CT imaging showed hepatosplenomegaly and generalized lymphadenopathy (Fig. 4f).
At 29 years of age, she presented with Raynaud’s phenomenon.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Both carriers have childhood-onset recurrent oral and genital ulcers with fever, the features the authors list as distinguishing HA20 from Behçet's disease. In the proband, exome sequencing found no variants in other autoinflammatory genes.

quotes.quote: We detected no variants in other genes associated with autoinflammatory diseases.
Applying these criteria, the clinical characteristics of our four patients were more consistent with HA20 than BD.

segregation.statement: The affected sister carries the variant (Sanger). Other affected or possibly affected relatives (elder brother with recurrent fever, father with oral ulcers and lymphadenopathy, paternal aunt with febrile episodes) are described, but the text does not say they were tested. The mother had no Behçet-like symptoms and died of colon cancer; her genotype is not reported.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the same variant in the affected sister (patient 2) (Fig. 1a).
The proband’s elder brother (III-1 in Fig. 1a) had multiple episodes of hospitalization due to the fever of unknown origin, but detailed clinical information is not available.
The proband’s father (II-5 in Fig. 1a) had recurrent oral ulcers.
The proband’s mother (II-6 in Fig. 1a) had no BD-like symptoms and passed away from colon cancer.
The proband’s aunt on the paternal side (II-2 in Fig. 1a) had recurrent febrile episodes, but details are unavailable.

functional.statement: RT-PCR on lymphoblastoid cell lines from patients 1 and 2 (patient cells): weaker band than control cells, stronger after cycloheximide; cycloheximide increased the mutant allele in sequenced RT-PCR products. The authors read this as the transcript possibly being subject to NMD. The control cDNA came from a patient with early-onset epilepsy.

quotes.quote: RT-PCR products were electrophoresed and the band intensity in DMSO-treated cells from affected patients was weak compared to that from DMSO-treated control cells.
Band intensity was stronger after CHX treatment (Fig. 2a).
Direct sequencing of PCR products showed that CHX treatment increased the presence of the mutant allele compared with DMSO treatment (Fig. 2b).
These results indicate that this nonsense variant may be subjected to NMD [23].
The control cDNA was isolated from a patient with a different disease (early-onset epilepsy).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense: c.1434C>A predicted p.(Cys478Ter). The paper describes HA20 as caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: Heterozygous loss-of-function TNFAIP3 variants identified in BD-like patients are now classified as haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) [5].

computational_predictions.statement: No specific scores or tools are given; the only in-silico mention is a criterion code within the authors' ACMG list.

quotes.quote: Based on the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines [24], this variant is classified as pathogenic (PVS1, PM2, PP3, PP4).

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from ExAC, from in-house exome controls and from Infevers, as stated by the authors.

quotes.quote: This variant was absent from ExAC, in-house exome controls, and Infevers (an online database for autoinflammatory mutations, https://infevers.umai-montpellier.fr/web).

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify the variant as pathogenic under ACMG (PVS1, PM2, PP3, PP4).

quotes.quote: Based on the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines [24], this variant is classified as pathogenic (PVS1, PM2, PP3, PP4).

concerns: The paper uses NM_006290.3; the batch HGVS is on NM_001270508.2. The protein agrees (protein_check: agrees).
Patients 1 and 2 are siblings in one family; they are two people, not a duplicate.
Several relatives with possible disease (father, elder brother, paternal aunt) have no stated genotype; the pedigree figure (Fig. 1a) is not available as text and may show more.
Zygosity is not stated in words in the text.
notes_for_panel: Two affected siblings in one family, both carriers. Functional data are RT-PCR on patient lymphoblastoid cells, consistent with NMD according to the authors. The authors give their own ACMG criteria.
